stem: A model for a die assumes that each of the six faces is equally likely. The die is thrown 150 times. Calculate the number of sixes the model predicts.
Which statement best describes a statistical model?

options.A: A collection of data taken from a sample of the population
options.B: A simplified mathematical description of a real situation, built on assumptions and used to make predictions
options.C: An exact copy of the real situation that includes every detail
options.D: A rule that guarantees exactly what will happen

stem: A council wants to find the mean weekly rent paid by all 4200 tenants in a town. It surveys 150 of the tenants, chosen at random. What is the population?

options.D: The weekly rents paid by the 150 tenants surveyed

stem: A model of a fair die predicts 10 sixes in 60 throws. A student throws the die 60 times and gets 7 sixes. Which conclusion is most reasonable?

options.A: The die is now more likely to give sixes, to make up the shortfall
options.B: The model is wrong because the count is not exactly 10
options.C: The difference is small enough to be chance variation, so there is no strong reason to reject the model
options.D: The model is proved correct, so the assumptions need no further checking

stem: The random variable $X$ is the score when a fair die is thrown. Which statement about $X$ is correct?

options.B: $X$ can take the values $1,2,\dots,6$ depending on the throw, and $x$ stands for one particular value
options.C: $X$ is an unknown number found by solving an equation
options.D: $X$ is the whole set of throws made by one student
